chapter_title: The Human is less than all the Things of the Unive
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶7:** The Divine Truth did not proceed forth and accomplish redemption solely for the sake of the human race, but [GAP-1] it proceeded and made itself manifest in the natural degree of the mind [GAP-2] its power prevailed outwardly in [GAP-3] the external orders of the spiritual world. And when it had completed its work of restoration throughout the outer reaches of the universal spiritual kingdom, it proceeded inward [GAP-4] it advanced still deeper into the most ancient celestial states of the will and understanding, and disclosed [GAP-5: interior wisdom to those primordial faculties].

**¶8:** They belong to the lineage of Divine wisdom and celestial good.

**¶9:** The successive states of [GAP-6: Divine wisdom in their fullness], the manner in which they unfold; and [GAP-7: the nature of] falsity from evil, how it too subsists as a perverted form.

**¶10:** The fullness of Divine wisdom — how it has operated against the dominion of falsity from evil, and subjugated it.

**¶11:** The Divine Truth came into the realm of spiritual death [GAP-8] — that is, the proprium, what is merely of the flesh-nature — so that it might recover what could be redeemed and bring those souls forth from the threshold of the hells below, for [GAP-9: they had] been engulfed into those infernal states.

**¶12:** The rebellious evils and falsities shall be restrained by a supreme bond of Divine order.

**¶16:** The Divine Truth in its redemptive suffering, which bears grief throughout the whole of creation, being present in both what pertains to the natural plane and what pertains to the spiritual plane — in all that is outwardly manifest and all that is interior and unseen.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Jesus did not come and s[a]ve the world because of mankind alone, but [also he] came and revealed on earth [and he] was strong outside in [the aeons] And [whe]n he had finished doing his [t]ask outside [i]n the great u[ni]verse, he came [down and he went]t further with Adam and Eve and revealed [to them].
they belong to the race of ligh[t].
the aeons [of the greatness], how they occur; and [the manner of] the darkness, how it t[o]o exists.
the [l]ight great-[ness], how it has been active against the pow[er of] darkness and conquered it.

he came to the province of death [and clothed himself in the body] that is flesh, until he should find profit and bring them from the gate of the underworld below, for [they had] been swa[ll]owed into it.
the rebels shall be bound in a great fetter
the Cross of Light, which g[rie]ves in the totality, being present in what is visible and what is not vis[ib]le.

fills.explanation: The text establishes that Jesus came not for mankind alone but ALSO for the broader cosmos; "also he" completes the contrastive construction "not... alone, but also he came."

The spiritual reading indicates a new clause ("its power prevailed outwardly"), requiring a subject connector to bridge "revealed on earth" with "was strong outside"; "and he" provides the conjunction and subject.

The spiritual reading's "external orders of the spiritual world" corresponds in Kephalaia vocabulary to "the aeons," the ordered cosmic emanations that are distinct from but encompassed by "the great universe" mentioned in the next clause.

The spiritual reading says "proceeded inward... advanced still deeper"; after finishing cosmic work in the great universe, Jesus "came down" (from the cosmic level to the Adamic level) and then "went further" into the most interior states with Adam and Eve.

The editor's "to them" correctly provides the indirect object for "revealed"; the spiritual reading's "interior wisdom" is already conveyed by "revealed" itself, and "those primordial faculties" = Adam and Eve already named, so "to them" is the necessary grammatical completion.

The spiritual reading's "Divine wisdom in their fullness" maps precisely to the standard Kephalaia phrase "the greatness" (Coptic: ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲟϭ), which denotes the divine pleroma; "the aeons of the greatness" is a fixed Manichaean expression for the divine emanated realms.

The editor's "the manner of" fits the parallel construction with the preceding clause ("the aeons... how they occur") and matches the spiritual reading's "the nature of"; "the manner of the darkness" is natural Kephalaia expository phrasing.

fills.fill: and clothed himself in the body
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading identifies the gap as introducing "the proprium" which "that is flesh" then glosses; in the Kephalaia's Manichaean register, the incarnation is expressed as clothing oneself in the body, and "the body that is flesh" provides the natural referent for the proprium.
The spiritual reading directly confirms "they had" as the correct subject and auxiliary verb before "been swallowed into it," referring to the souls engulfed in the infernal states.
